stem_text: A particle (m = 1 kg) slides down a frictionless track (AOC) starting from rest at a point A (height 2 m). After reaching C, the particle continues to move freely in air as a projectile. When it reaches its highest point P (height 1 m), the kinetic energy of the particle (in J) is : (Figure drawn is schematic and not to scale; take g = 10 ms-2) [FIG-stem-1]

candidate_solve.derivation: Mass m = 1 kg, g = 10 m/s^2. Since track is frictionless and air resistance is absent, mechanical energy is conserved throughout. E_total = K_A + U_A = 0 + m*g*h_A = 1 * 10 * 2 = 20 J. At apex point P (height h_P = 1 m): U_P = m*g*h_P = 1 * 10 * 1 = 10 J. Kinetic energy at P: K_P = E_total - U_P = 20 - 10 = 10 J.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Conservation of total mechanical energy in conservative gravitational field

representation_translation.evidence: Reading elevation coordinates hA = 2 m and hP = 1 m from schematic track and projectile description

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Direct energy conservation: KE_P = E_initial - PE_P = mg(hA - hP)

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Recognizing intermediate track profile AOC and launch projectile angle are superfluous

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying mechanical energy conservation across elevation points
